newsitem.title: USA: Scholastic is sued by shareholder group.
newsitem.headline: Scholastic is sued by shareholder group.

text.p: Certain shareholders of Scholastic Corp said Tuesday they had sued the company, alleging that false statements by the company had inflated Scholastic's stock price.

Laywers for the plaintiffs said the suit, filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, was brought on behalf of those who bought Scholastic stock between December 6, 1996, and February 20, 1997.

The suit alleges that the company disseminated numerous announcements concerning its financial success and expansion during the period in question, and the statements caused Scholastic's stock price to rise to a high of $78.

It alleges the statements were materially false and misleading because they failed to disclose high book returns requiring reserves and a special charge to earnings, decreased demand, and inadequate operating controls to account for returns.
The complaint alleges that while these problems were concealed, certain officers and directors sold, immediately before and during the class period, over 77,000 shares of Scholastic common stock.
Plaintiffs seek unspecified damages and are represented by the law offices Bernard M. Gross PC and Bernstein Litowitz Berger and Grossmann Llp.
Scholastic officials could not be reached for comment.
